evidence.excerpt: Cutting-plan scheduling in textile manufacturing requires allocating pattern-piece layouts to fabric rolls while respecting roll length, colour lot constraints, and due-date windows for garment assembly. This paper proposes a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model that integrates roll assignment, layout sequencing, and spread-height decisions. The model is tested on data from a mid-sized Serbian garment manufacturer with 12-week planning horizons and up to 85 active orders simultaneously. A column generation approach decomposes the problem into a master scheduling problem and a subproblem equivalent to a weighted bin-packing instance. On instances with up to 40 orders, the column generation procedure closes 94% of the LP relaxation gap within 600 seconds. Material utilisation improved from 78.2% to 81.9% compared to the company's manual planning procedure, and roll inventory turnover increased by 11% over a three-month pilot. Limitations regarding shade-banding constraints are discussed.
